# contracts — agent brief

## Purpose
contracts is the platform's shared schema kernel: every cross-hexagon port as OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema, with Java, TypeScript and Python bindings that consumers pin by Git tag (D031).
It is not a service: no runtime, no business logic. It never fixes another repo; it raises a demand instead.
Description: [hexagon page](../documentations/reference/hexagons/contracts.md) · [HEXAGON.md](HEXAGON.md)

## Build, test, run
pip install jsonschema pyyaml
python tests/run_all.py
mvn -f $PWD/gen/java/pom.xml test | grep 'Tests run'
cd gen/ts && npm ci && npx tsc --noEmit
# regenerate bindings: per-language commands in DEPLOYMENT.md (python-regen-procedure)
# publish: git push origin main vX.Y.Z && git ls-remote --tags origin | grep vX.Y.Z
# then: git worktree add --detach ../contracts-worktrees/vX.Y.Z vX.Y.Z

## Top gotchas
- **A tag is released only once it is on origin** — A tag is released only once it is on origin Consumers pin the GitHub tag (D031). Push it yourself with git push origin main vX.Y.Z, then confirm git ls-remote --tags origin | grep vX.Y.Z and that git ls-remote origin main matches HEAD. If you cannot push, report blocked, not done. On 2026-10-27 a report claimed v0.64.0 done while origin stopped at v0.63.0, so its D031 install could not have run. Before tagging, compare git tag with git ls-remote --tags origin: a prior release (e.g. v0.66.0) may exist only locally. Push it in the same git push as the new tag; do not re-point it. ([note](.brain/notes/verify-release-tag-on-origin.md))
- **Strict tsc acceptance: use bundler resolution** — In the TS acceptance, run tsc with --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler. The installed tsc rejects --moduleResolution node10 (TS5108, removed) and node16 paired with --module commonjs (TS5110). Passing combos: --module esnext --target es2022 --moduleResolution bundler, or --module node16 --moduleResolution node16. Do not spend retries on the old flags. ([note](.brain/notes/tsc-flags-for-strict-acceptance.md))
- **npx tsc resolves to a squatter package** — Never run npx tsc in a scratch project; install typescript there and use its tsc. In a scratch project, npx resolves 'tsc' to an unrelated squatter package, and the acceptance fails for no real reason. Inside gen/ts, npm ci installs typescript first, so npx tsc --noEmit is safe there. ([note](.brain/notes/npx-tsc-is-a-squatter.md))
- **CHANGELOG.md and gen/ts/index.ts are cp1252, index.ts is CRLF** — Edit CHANGELOG.md and gen/ts/index.ts as bytes (latin-1 round trip), not as UTF-8 text. Both files contain cp1252 bytes, so read and write them with encoding='latin-1'. gen/ts/index.ts also uses CRLF line endings: keep them. Its line 1 says v0.1.0, but that comment is stale and is not the version. ([note](.brain/notes/cp1252-and-crlf-files.md))
- **progress-frozen validator checks history, not the file** — progress-frozen fails on commit history; restoring PROGRESS.md does not clear it The conventions validator v2 check progress-frozen inspects commit history after the freeze commit (803eb1b), not the current file. If a later commit touched PROGRESS.md below its freeze header, the check keeps failing even when a commit restores the file byte-identical to the freeze commit. Do not spend time on restoring commits. The only fixes are rewriting history on main or changing the validator in the conventions repo; both need an owner or architect decision. Write a fulfillment report with status: blocked that includes the validator output, and do not push. ([note](.brain/notes/progress-frozen-checks-history.md))
